evals.prompt: Clean up the commits on this branch before I open a PR. It has 3 logical commits plus 2 `fixup!` commits from addressing review feedback.
evals.expected_output: Skill auto-triggers and takes the Step 3a autosquash path (not the full soft-reset rewrite): verifies each fixup's target commit actually contains the patched lines, asks for confirmation before the irreversible rebase, then runs `git rebase -i --autosquash`.

expectations.name: skill-invoked
expectations.description: rewrite-commits loads for the commit-cleanup request
expectations.check: Transcript shows the rewrite-commits skill loaded

expectations.name: prefers-autosquash-for-fixups
expectations.description: Chooses the Step 3a autosquash path because fixup! commits exist
expectations.check: Transcript shows `git rebase -i --autosquash` and does NOT do a `git reset --soft` full rewrite

expectations.name: verifies-fixup-target
expectations.description: Confirms each fixup's target contains the patched lines before squashing
expectations.check: Output references checking the target commit (e.g. `git log ... -- <path>` or `git show <target>`)

expectations.name: confirms-before-rewrite
expectations.description: Asks the user to confirm before the irreversible autosquash rebase
expectations.check: Transcript shows a proposal/confirmation step before running the rebase

evals.prompt: My branch is messy — about 8 WIP commits with messages like 'wip', 'fix', 'more', 'oops'. Reorganize them into clean logical commits before the PR.
evals.expected_output: Skill auto-triggers, proposes logical commit splits for approval, and uses the Step 4 soft-reset path (`git reset --soft` to the merge base, then re-create commits) — autosquash does not apply because there are no fixup! commits.

expectations.name: skill-invoked
expectations.description: rewrite-commits loads for the messy-history request
expectations.check: Transcript shows the rewrite-commits skill loaded

expectations.name: proposes-logical-splits
expectations.description: Presents a proposed commit grouping and waits for approval
expectations.check: Output presents proposed commits and asks the user to approve before rewriting

expectations.name: uses-soft-reset
expectations.description: Uses the soft-reset rewrite path, not autosquash (no fixups present)
expectations.check: Output contains `git reset --soft` against the merge base

evals.prompt: I ran `git rebase -i --autosquash` and it hit a conflict with `<<<<<<< HEAD`, an empty section, then `>>>>>>> <my fixup sha>`. What went wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Skill explains the fixup was targeted at a commit that does not yet contain the patched lines, and gives the correct recovery: abort, re-identify the right target, un-commit the mis-targeted fixup with `git reset --soft`, re-create it with `git commit --fixup`, retry. It must NOT suggest `git commit --amend --fixup` (invalid — mutually exclusive flags).

expectations.name: explains-misaimed-fixup
expectations.description: Identifies the cause as a fixup aimed at a commit lacking the patched lines
expectations.check: Output explains the target commit does not contain the lines the fixup patches

expectations.name: correct-recovery-sequence
expectations.description: Recovery uses abort + reset --soft + commit --fixup, then retry
expectations.check: Output contains `git rebase --abort` and `git reset --soft` and `git commit --fixup`

expectations.name: no-invalid-amend-fixup
expectations.description: Does not propose the invalid `git commit --amend --fixup`

evals.prompt: Can you squash and reword the commits on this branch? Heads up — it's already pushed and a teammate has branched off it with work in progress on top.
evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes this is shared, already-pushed history with dependent work and does NOT rewrite. It warns that rewriting would break the teammate's branch and offers a non-destructive alternative (e.g. a follow-up commit) instead of reset/rebase.

expectations.name: refuses-to-rewrite-shared-history
expectations.description: Does not run reset --soft / rebase on a shared pushed branch with dependents
expectations.check: Transcript shows the skill declines to rewrite and does NOT run git reset --soft or git rebase

expectations.name: warns-about-dependents
expectations.description: Explains the risk to the teammate's branched work
expectations.check: Output warns that rewriting shared history breaks others' branches

evals.prompt: Prepare my branch for a PR — tidy up the commit history if it needs it.
evals.expected_output: After inspecting the branch and finding a single, well-formatted conventional commit, the skill reports there is nothing to reorganize and stops, rather than forcing an unnecessary rewrite.

expectations.name: detects-already-clean
expectations.description: Inspects commits and recognizes the history is already clean before acting
expectations.check: Transcript shows the skill checked the commit list (e.g. git log) before deciding

expectations.name: stops-without-rewriting
expectations.description: States nothing to rewrite and does not run a destructive rewrite
expectations.check: Output says the history is already clean / nothing to do and runs no git reset --soft or rebase
